# Overview of the *Whole-Child and Family Supports Inventory* in Year 3

This section of the APR captures the range and alignment of academic, social-emotional, health, and family supports available to students and families. The questions are designed to assess how well these supports are coordinated and responsive to local needs and assets.

The 27 supports in the inventory are divided into six categories, according to the nature of the support and the roles in the school community that engage with that support: Integrated Student Supports and Services; Community, Student & Family Engagement; Collaborative Leadership Practices; Expanded & Enriched Learning Time; Community-based Curriculum & Pedagogy, and; Positive & Restorative School Climate. Each category is presented in a different section below. For each support identified under the category, grantees were asked to identify those that were part of their implementation plan.

## I. Integrated Student Supports and Services

::: panel-tabset
### A. Availability/Presence

In Year 3, 87% of grantees indicated that Mental Health Screening Services were part of their implementation plan. Multi-Tiered System of Support were identified by 84% of grantees as a critical offering.

![](images/IA.png){fig-align="center"}

### B. Implementation of the Supports/Service

A majority of the Integrated Student Supports and Services offered by grantees in Year 3 were previously offered prior to the CCSPP and integrated into their community schools work. Over 80% of grantees indicated that they previously implemented each of the supports. One exception is the Coordination of Services Team (e.g., COST team), with 25% of grantees indicating that implementation was the result of CCSPP funding.

![](images/IB.png){fig-align="center"}

### C. Served individuals by Support/Service

Grantees were asked the number of individuals that were served by each support. In Year 3 of the CCSPP Implementation Grant, for those support that are grouped around the presence of integrated student supports and services, it is possible to see that *...*.

![](images/IC.png){fig-align="center"}

### D. Support/Service funding 

To fund these supports and services, grantees were asked to report funding sources beyond CCSPP to sustain the support long-term. Grantees tapped into traditional funding sources, such as *LCFF to support their Multi-Tiered System of Support (25% of grantees)* and *Title I to support offerings of Academic Supports (14% of grantees) and the Multi-Tiered System of Support.* *Expanded Learning Opportunities Program (ELOP) is also used to support offerings of Academic Supports (15% of Grantees)*.

![](images/ID.png){fig-align="center"}
:::

## II. Community, Student, and Family Engagement

::: panel-tabset
### A. Overview of the Presence of the Support in Year 3

Grantees were asked for each support to mention those that were part of their implementation of Community Schools. In Year 3 of the CCSPP Implementation Grant, for those support that are grouped around Community, Student, and Family Engagement, it is possible to see that *90% of grantees mention implementing Multiple Modes of Family Communication and Involvement*. In addition, it's relevant to note that *67% of grantees mention implementing Home Visits*.

![](images/IIA.png){fig-align="center"}

### B. CCSPP Implementation of the Supports in Year 3

Grantees were asked when did they start implementing each support. In Year 3 of the CCSPP Implementation Grant, for those support that are grouped around Community, Student, and Family Engagement, it is possible to see that *32% of grantees mention starting the implementation of Adult Education programs exclusively as a result of CCSPP*.

![](images/IIB.png){fig-align="center"}

### C. Served individuals by support in Year 3

Grantees were asked the number of individuals that were served by each support. In Year 3 of the CCSPP Implementation Grant, for those support that are grouped around Community, Student, and Family Engagement, it is possible to see that *NA*

![](images/IIC.png){fig-align="center"}

### D. Supports funding in Year 3

Grantees were asked the indicate the funding sources that helped them leverage each support. In Year 3 of the CCSPP Implementation Grant, for those support that are grouped around Community, Student, and Family Engagement, it is possible to see that *LCFF is used frequently to fund the Multiple Modes of Family Communication and Involvement and also Home Visits*.

![](images/IID.png){fig-align="center"}
:::

## III. Collaborative Leadership Practices

::: panel-tabset
### A. Overview of the Presence of the Support in Year 3

Grantees were asked for each support to mention those that were part of their implementation of Community Schools. In Year 3 of the CCSPP Implementation Grant, for those support that are grouped around collaborative leadership practices, it is possible to see that *89% of grantees have implemented a shared decision-making body that center the voices of all community members, including students, families, and other stakeholders*.

![](images/IIIA.png){fig-align="center"}

### B. CCSPP Implementation of the Supports in Year 3

Grantees were asked when did they start implementing each support. In Year 3 of the CCSPP Implementation Grant, for those support that are grouped around collaborative leadership practices, it is possible to see that *31% of grantees started implementing Parent Leadership Development Opportunities exlusively because the CCSPP funding*. In addition, *28% of grantees mention starting the Shared decision-making bodies exclusively as a result of CCSPP funding*.

![](images/IIIB.png){fig-align="center"}

### C. Served individuals by support in Year 3

Grantees were asked the number of individuals that were served by each support. In Year 3 of the CCSPP Implementation Grant, for those support that are grouped around collaborative leadership practices, it is possible to see that *...*.

![](images/IIIC.png){fig-align="center"}

### D. Supports funding in Year 3

Grantees were asked the indicate the funding sources that helped them leverage each support. In Year 3 of the CCSPP Implementation Grant, for those support that are grouped around collaborative leadership practices, it is possible to see that *Teacher Leadership Development and Opportunities is being funded by a diversity of sources --such as LCFF, General Funds, Title I, among others*. In addition, the newly implemented *Shared Decision-Making Bodies are being funded by many sources, including the LCFF, General Funds, Title I funds, and District Funds*.

![](images/IIID.png){fig-align="center"}
:::
